A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, Tree Search for Language Model Agents. Text, equations, figures, tables and Appendix A support a complete comparison; v4's reduction from 26 to 25 pages reflects repagination, not missing material.

before.justification: v3 reports original WebArena and VisualWebArena experiments, including search-versus-no-search results in Table 2 and ablations in Section 5 and Appendix A.2.

after.justification: v4 retains these original benchmark experiments, search ablations, model comparisons and qualitative agent trajectories.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and A.4 retain the same best-first search, model-based value function, branching, backtracking and termination procedures. Algorithm 1 is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 910 VisualWebArena tasks, 812 WebArena tasks and 200-task VisualWebArena ablation subset. Website coverage and qualitative test scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within Tables 2, 4 and 8 and Figure 3, including no-search agents, published web-agent baselines, alternative value functions and trajectory reranking.

E3.justification: Both retain the same success-rate evaluation, action limits, search defaults of depth 5, branching factor 5 and budget 20, sampling settings and ablation configurations.

E4.justification: The search-budget, tree-size and value-function ablations, trajectory-reranking comparison, difficulty and website breakdowns, and qualitative examples are unchanged in Section 5 and Appendix A.1–A.2.

E5.justification: Both retain the same point-estimate success-rate reporting, without experimental confidence intervals, significance tests or seed-based variability estimates. Sampling and trajectory-count information is also unchanged.

E6.justification: All matched numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged. Examples include GPT-4o search success rates of 26.4% on VisualWebArena and 19.2% on WebArena in Table 2, and 37.0% on the ablation subset in Table 3.

T1.justification: The environment and transition definitions, value-function formulation and search-update equations in Sections 2–3 are identical. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same novelty claim, benchmark improvement claims, compatibility with existing agents and test-time-compute scaling claim.

C2.justification: Interpretations of search gains and value-function quality remain unchanged, as do limitations concerning computation, destructive actions and domain-specific value functions in Section 5.4.

D1.justification: Sections 4.1 and A.3–A.4 retain the same model identifiers, prompts, viewport dimensions, observation truncation, sampling settings and environment-reset instructions. Code and model access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to prior web-agent and search research are unchanged. The reference list is repaginated without additions or removals.

P1.justification: The arXiv margin stamp changes from v3 dated 24 September 2025 to v4 dated 8 February 2026. The paper's wording, section hierarchy and narrative order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 fills the large blank area on v3 page 9 with the existing Figure 3, reranking analysis and subsequent breakdown. Later figures, tables and references reflow, and the appendix begins one page earlier. Display contents and captions are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 corrects the conspicuous unused space on v3 page 9 by bringing existing analysis and Figure 3 forward, providing a modest presentation improvement. The scientific argument, experimental evidence, limitations and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
